title: Line up the chute gates for the green bin, then release the batch
instruction: Set the two grey chute gates so the balls run into the green bin, then pull the orange slide gate open and hold it until all three have left the hopper.
context: Conveyor operators and tenders set diverter gates by hand to route a batch to the right bin, then open a slide gate to run it (O*NET 53-7011.00 Conveyor Operators and Tenders). Order matters because material cannot be recalled once it has left the hopper. Board chute tasks (parcels into chutes by a routing card, single-file induction) have the robot place or space parcels; here it sets the path and the balls do the rest.
setup: Positions are object centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left (negative toward the right arm). Table: wood top, about 110 x 130 cm, arm bases 61 cm apart (y +30.5 and -30.5) on its near edge. Everything below is fixed except the three gate sliders and the balls. Chute: dark plywood ramp 37 x 23 x 1 cm (x 13 to 50, y -11.5 to +11.5), tilted 8 degrees with its low end toward the arms: top 4.2 cm above the table at x 13, 9.4 cm at x 50; four 2 x 2 cm legs at x 15 and 49 and a 1 cm face at the low end hold it. White plywood side walls, 1 cm thick and 5 cm tall (square to the ramp), inner faces at y -10 and +10; where the gates pass, a low rail 1 cm tall replaces the wall: left side x 26.8 to 41, right side x 18.5 to 29.5. Two white dividers 5 x 1 x 5 cm at y -3.5 and +3.5, x 13 to 18, make three lanes. Hopper: blue plywood box on the ramp, x 39.5 to 48.5, y -3.5 to +3.5, 4.5 cm tall, roofed and closed except its mouth at x 39.5 (5 cm wide, 3.5 cm high inside); the roof has a 2 cm wide slot along its length, so the balls show from above but cannot pass. Balls: three yellow hardwood balls, 2.5 cm across, 30 g, in a row at y 0, x 40.5, 43.0 and 45.5, the first against the slide gate. Bins on the table at the low end, x 5 to 13, white walls 1 cm thick and 7 cm tall, back wall at x 4 to 5: left y +4 to +10 with a grey floor, middle y -3 to +3 grey floor, right y -10 to -4 green floor (floors 2 mm thick). Left gate (grey slick plastic, slides along y, travel 9 cm, no spring, damped): bar 13 x 1.2 x 3.8 cm tall standing 1.2 cm over the ramp, from x 36.5, y -3 to x 28, y +7, so the balls run to the left grey bin; a rod 1.2 cm thick, 9.5 to 10.4 cm above the table, leads over the wall to an upright handle 4 x 3 x 5 cm (x 28 to 32, y 13 to 16, 9.5 to 14.5 cm up). Pulled 8.5 cm or more to +y it clears the balls. Right gate (grey, same slide): mirror bar from x 28, y -5 to x 19.5, y -15 at rest, out toward the right wall, with its handle 4 x 3 x 5 cm at x 18 to 22, y -16.5 to -13.5 (9.5 to 14.5 cm up). Pushed 8.5 cm or more to +y (bar from x 28, y +4 to x 19.5, y -6) it sends the balls to the green bin. Slide gate (orange, travel 6.5 cm, spring of 60 N/m pulling it shut, damped): plate 1.5 x 7 x 3.8 cm tall over the ramp across the hopper mouth, x 37.9 to 39.4, y -3 to +4, with a rod at 9.5 to 10.4 cm up to an upright handle 4 x 3 x 5 cm at x 35.5 to 39.5, y 13 to 16. Handles and rods stay above the balls (underside 9.5 cm up).
scoring: Photo and tape measure. Count the balls resting in the green bin (centre x 5 to 14, y -10 to -4, under 4 cm high, still, on its floor or on another ball there). A ball that was ever over a grey bin, at any height, is lost and never counts. Score 0 if a ball is ever lifted out over the bins (centre over 7 cm up). Otherwise: 1.0 for three balls with the slide gate shut (handle within 5 mm of its start); 0.75 for three with it open, or two; 0.5 for one; 0.25 for none, if no ball is lost and both grey gates are set (each handle moved 8.5 cm or more from its start); else 0. A ball held in the air counts as not placed.
reset_notes: Push the left gate back across the chute, pull the right gate out beyond the wall, and let the slide gate spring shut. Pick the balls out of the bins and put them back in a row in the hopper against the slide gate (pull the gate open a little, drop them in through the mouth, release). Mark each handle's start on the table.
fidelity: Rigid balls on a rigid 8-degree chute; rolling, bounces and bin settling are the simulator's, so timing is approximate. Gates are slides with end stops; the slide gate has a 60 N/m spring. The simulator scores the final step without opening the grippers, so a ball still held counts as not placed (underside over 1 cm above every support) and a ball over a grey bin at any height is lost.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (moved right arm toward the chute and hovered, gates and balls stayed unchanged); demo: 1.0 (pulled both gates into place, opened slide gate, balls rolled into green bin, arms let go)
